methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study of 84 LACC patients with immunohistochemical biomarker analysis and survival correlation. Blinded scoring by two gynecological oncologists. Appropriate statistical methods: Kaplan-Meier survival curves, Cox proportional hazards regression, Pearson correlation, Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis for quantitative variables. RECIST-based response evaluation (92.9% response rate). However, limited sample size (N=84), single-institution retrospective design, and FFPE samples limit generalizability. Multivariate analysis shows no independent associations (Table II), suggesting potential confounding.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective observational case-cohort study mapping to LoE 3b. Clinical population (LACC patients treated with concurrent chemoradiation), outcome-driven (OS/DFS), and biomarker assessment (SETD2, GLI1 by IHC). Direct relevance to treatment-resistant cervical cancer. However, mechanism-based evidence limited to expression-only analysis; no functional validation or therapeutic targeting of GLI1/SETD2 pathway. Association with hormonal contraceptive use identified but causality unexplored.

reporting_quality.justification: Biomarker study with IHC assay details: antibody sources/catalog numbers, IS calculation methodology (percentage × intensity), scoring criteria defined. REMARK-adjacent reporting for prognostic marker study. However, key REMARK items incomplete: no pre-specification of IS threshold (cutoff IS >6 appears post-hoc optimized rather than pre-specified); tissue source redacted in Methods ('patients who [REDACTED] and December 2018'); no statement on data availability or sample allocation; supplementary tables and figures referenced but content not provided in normalized text.

novelty_literature.justification: Hedgehog/GLI1 pathway and its role in cervical cancer chemoradiation resistance previously established (refs. 10-14, 24-26). SETD2 mutations and epigenetic dysregulation in cervical cancer known. Authors claim 'first to investigate the association between SETD2 and GLI1 expression and localization' but this represents incremental extension of known pathway components to a new biomarker pair. No new mechanism, pathway discovery, or therapeutic intervention. HPV genotype-SETD2 correlation is modest novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is well-organized with clear Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Clinical context and prior mechanistic understanding appropriately framed. Results systematically presented with IS values, survival curves, and multivariate models. Discussion contextualizes findings against prior Hh pathway work and addresses HPV genotype interactions. However, Methods contain redacted text (tissue source), and supplementary materials referenced but not fully available. Some mechanistic speculation (estrogenic stimulation via GSK3β) extends beyond data presented.

key_strengths: Clinically relevant population (84 LACC patients with known outcomes) with rigorous survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, Cox proportional hazards) and median 53-month follow-up
Blinded scoring by two gynecological pathologists with concordance assessment minimizes observer bias

Dual-protein analysis (SETD2 and GLI1) with cellular localization specificity (nuclear vs. cytoplasmic) provides mechanistic differentiation—nGLI1 IS >6 predicts worse OS/DFS while ncGLI1 IS >6 predicts better OS
HPV genotyping identifies differential SETD2 expression (HPV18/other vs. HPV16), suggesting genotype-epigenetic interactions
key_concerns: Limited sample size (N=84) with single-center, retrospective design reduces external validity; multivariate analysis (Table II) reveals no independent associations, suggesting confounding by TNM stage or treatment factors
REMARK adherence incomplete: IS threshold (>6) appears post-hoc optimized rather than pre-specified; no explanation for threshold selection; data availability statement absent
Mechanistic novelty limited: Hh/GLI1 role in cervical CRT resistance established; SETD2-GLI1 correlation is descriptive without functional validation or pathway inhibition studies

No multivariate adjustment for key prognostic factors (FIGO stage, lymph node status, tumor grade, HPV type); univariate HRs show wide confidence intervals (e.g., nGLI1: 1.44–14.13), indicating statistical instability
Causality between oral contraceptive use, estrogenic stimulation, and GLI1 nuclear translocation remains speculative; no mechanistic experiments
Methods redaction ('patients who [REDACTED] and December 2018') impedes reproducibility assessment; supplementary materials not provided
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective biomarker study in clinically relevant LACC population with rigorous survival analysis but limited mechanistic novelty and sample size. Appropriate for specialized journals with major revisions addressing confounding, REMARK compliance, and pre-specification of biomarker thresholds.
